title: Armenia returns four border villages to Azerbaijan in the first delimitation step
body:
On 24 May 2024 Armenia's security service said its border guards had taken up new positions after Armenia returned four villages in its northeastern Tavush region to Azerbaijan. The villages were Baghanis, Voskepar, Kirants and Berkaber, known in Azerbaijan as Baghanis Ayrum, Asagi Eskipara, Heyrimli and Kizilhacili. They were uninhabited and had been seized by Armenia in the 1990s. On 16 May the two countries had redrawn 12.7 kilometres of borderland, and Azerbaijan's Deputy Prime Minister Shahin Mustafayev confirmed that Azerbaijani border guards had taken control of the settlements.

Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan called the deal a milestone toward peace. Azerbaijan had demanded the villages' return as a condition for a peace deal. The villages lie near Armenia's main highway north toward Georgia, which carries much of the country's trade and a Russian gas pipeline.

Weeks of antigovernment protests followed, with thousands of demonstrators led by Archbishop Bagrat Galstanyan accusing Pashinyan of betrayal and demanding his resignation. Residents of nearby settlements said the transfer could cut them off from the rest of Armenia. Other territorial disputes, mostly over enclaves, remained unresolved.
